name: const unsafe fn transmute < Src , Dst > (src : Src) -> Dst
rule: A pointer constructed by transmuting an integer to a pointer must not be used for non-zero-sized memory accesses; such accesses are currently considered undefined behavior. This also applies when the integer is nested inside an array, tuple, struct, or enum.
api: const unsafe fn transmute < Src , Dst > (src : Src) -> Dst
expression: This requirement cannot be expressed in the supplied DSL: it cannot identify integer-to-pointer transmutations, including nested ones, or quantify over subsequent memory accesses.
